title: Middle East Crude Exports Surpass Pre-War Levels Even as Tanker Attacks Continue Rising
detail: Middle East crude oil exports have recovered to exceed pre-war levels, signaling a partial normalization of supply chains. However, tanker attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz continue to rise, presenting a dual-trend dynamic: supply volumes are recovering while maritime security risks remain elevated. Analysts note the divergence underscores the resilience of alternative routing options and increased naval escorts, but warn that sustained attack escalation could reverse the export recovery if insurers withdraw coverage or shippers divert to longer routes.

title: Iran-Linked Forces Strike 11 Vessels in Strait of Hormuz in Single Week
detail: Iran-linked forces have struck 11 vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz within a single week, representing a sharp escalation in attack tempo. The surge marks a significant intensification compared to prior weekly averages and raises concerns about sustained disruption to oil and food commodity shipments through the world's most critical maritime chokepoint.

title: Al Jazeera: Iran Effectively Charging 'Toll' for Oil Traffic Through Hormuz
detail: Al Jazeera investigates whether Iran is now effectively charging a de facto 'toll' for oil tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, raising questions about unprecedented Iranian leverage over global energy shipping. The analysis highlights how systematic vessel interdiction combined with selective passage has given Iran coercive influence over crude flows, affecting food and commodity supply chains dependent on maritime routes through the strait.
